newsitem.title: UK: Britain to ban keeping handguns at home - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Britain to ban keeping handguns at home - newspaper.

text.p: Britain is to ban weapons enthusiasts from keeping their handguns at home following the Dunblane school massacre in which 16 children and their teacher were killed in March, the Sunday Times newspaper said.

"Ministers...acknowledge that a new law obliging handguns to be stored permanently at a gun club is the least restriction that the gun lobby should expect," the newspaper said, citing unnamed government sources.

Lord Cullen, a senior judge, was appointed to head an inquiry into the Dunblane killings and to consider possible new gun laws. He is due to present his recommendations to Scottish minister Michael Forsyth on Monday.
The Dunblane killer, Thomas Hamilton, held licences for the four semi-automatic handguns he used in Britain's worst gun massacre, even though he was widely regarded as a social misfit.
Opinion polls show 70 percent in Britain want handguns to be banned, but the influential gun lobby says this would be an infringement of liberties and would not prevent future gun crimes anyway.

The Sunday Times said that if Cullen recommends a total ban on handguns the government will comply, but that whatever his report said, ministers had agreed a ban on keeping such weapons at home was "the minimum necessary" to reassure the public.

"A ban on home ownership is the prime minister's (John Major) preferred option. A complete ban would never get through the Commons (lower house of parliament)," the newspaper quoted a source as saying.
